# Parser fixtures (independent, hand-written)

These fixtures exist because the legacy `tools/log_aggregator.py` docstring warns
that its parser test data was generated by the same parser logic, so the tests
could false-pass when real archived log formats drift. The lines here are written
by hand to mirror representative production log shapes and are **not** produced by
the parser code, so they validate the parsers against independent input.

## Files

| File | Format | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `json_logs.log` | JSON lines | Structured logs using the alternate key names the parser supports (`timestamp`/`time`/`@timestamp`, `level`/`severity`/`lvl`, `service`/`logger`/`app`, `message`/`msg`/`event`), including one numeric epoch timestamp. |
| `text_logs.log` | plain text | Common application/syslog-style lines: `ISO-ish timestamp`, bracketed service, level keyword, and one line with no metadata at all. |
| `nginx_logs.log` | nginx combined access log | `$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" $status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" "$http_user_agent"`, covering 2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx so the level mapping is exercised. |
| `malformed_logs.log` | mixed / garbage | Truncated JSON, unstructured junk, a random text line, a JSON record with an unparseable timestamp, and a blank line. None of these may crash parsing. |

## Intent

* `json_logs.log`, `text_logs.log`, `nginx_logs.log` are the "known good"
  formats; `tools/tests/test_log_aggregator_fixtures.py` asserts the extracted
  timestamp, level, service/format and key format-specific fields.
* `malformed_logs.log` verifies graceful handling: malformed or unsupported
  lines are skipped (or fall through to the generic text parser) without raising,
  and a blank line is ignored.

The timestamps in these fixtures are all in UTC so the expected epoch values are
unambiguous. Fixture lines are intentionally realistic enough to catch
regressions when the parsers are changed.
